metric_identity.metric_name: State of AI Report 2025 — Independent annual report covering AI research breakthroughs, industry commercialization, geopolitics, and safety across 313 slides with inaugural practitioner survey
metric_identity.source_report: State of AI Report 2025, 8th edition, produced by Nathan Benaich (Air Street Capital) and Ian Hogarth
metric_identity.methodology_notes: Annual independent report now in its eighth edition, reviewed by leading AI practitioners in industry and research. Covers four key dimensions: Research (technology breakthroughs and capabilities), Industry (commercial applications and business impact), Politics (regulation, economic implications, and geopolitics), and Safety (catastrophic risk identification and mitigation). The 2025 edition introduces the first State of AI Usage Survey of 1,200 AI practitioners covering adoption patterns, spending, and productivity impact. The report comprises 313 slides compiled from publicly available research papers, industry data, benchmark leaderboards, policy documents, and direct survey responses. Data collection spans the 12 months preceding publication. Available as a free Google Slides presentation and companion Substack post.

metric_value.value: Multiple key metrics: (1) 44% of US businesses now pay for AI tools (up from 5% in 2023); (2) Average AI contract value reached $530,000 in 2025, expected to pass $1M in 2026; (3) AI-first companies growing 1.5x faster than peers; (4) 95% of surveyed AI practitioners use AI at work or home; (5) 76% of practitioners pay for AI tools out of pocket; (6) 92% of practitioners report productivity gains from AI; (7) Qwen accounts for over 40% of new monthly model derivatives on Hugging Face; (8) Llama's share of model derivatives cratered from ~50% to 15%; (9) By 2030, top supercomputers may need 2 million chips, $200B investment, and 9 GW of power; (10) DeepSeek-R1 outperformed OpenAI o1 on multiple key reasoning benchmarks
metric_value.unit: Multiple units: percentage, USD, multiplier, count, gigawatts
metric_value.geographic_scope: Global, with specific breakdowns for US, China, and EU
metric_value.comparison_baseline: AI tool adoption by US businesses: 5% in 2023 (now 44% in 2025, an 8.8x increase); Llama HuggingFace model derivative share: ~50% previously (now 15%); Qwen model derivative share grew to 40%+ from a smaller base; OpenAI maintained frontier lead but gap narrowed significantly with Chinese models
metric_value.market_layer: cross-cutting (covers infrastructure through compute and power, model layer through frontier labs and open-weights, application layer through enterprise adoption, and vertical through scientific and robotics applications)

trend.year_over_year_change: US business AI adoption: 5% to 44% over 2 years (~8.8x); Average AI contract value reached $530K heading toward $1M+; Practitioner AI usage near-universal at 95%; China open-weights ecosystem surged (Qwen 40%+ of HuggingFace derivatives, DeepSeek-R1 surpassed o1); Llama's open-source dominance declined from ~50% to 15%; Infrastructure spending entering trillion-dollar territory; AI safety deprioritized as labs missed self-imposed safety deadlines
trend.forecast_value: Average AI contract value expected to exceed $1M in 2026; Top supercomputers may require $200B investment and 9 GW of power by 2030; Data center infrastructure projected to require ~$500B capital investment annually
trend.velocity_indicator: adoption_doubling_time: US business AI adoption went from 5% to 44% in approximately 2 years; AI-first company growth rate 1.5x faster than peers; China's model performance gap with US narrowing rapidly (DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi approaching parity on reasoning and coding benchmarks)

entrepreneurial_relevance.relevance_for_entrepreneurs: This is the most widely read independent annual AI report globally, offering founders a comprehensive landscape view. Key signals for entrepreneurs: (1) The explosion from 5% to 44% in US businesses paying for AI tools in two years indicates the enterprise AI market has crossed the chasm from early adopters to early majority — the window for market entry is narrowing but revenue opportunity is massive; (2) Average contract values of $530K heading to $1M+ signal that enterprise AI is not a low-ticket SaaS play but a high-value category; (3) China's open-weights ecosystem overtaking Llama (Qwen at 40%+ of HuggingFace derivatives) means founders building on open-source models now have a geopolitical choice with real implications for enterprise compliance and trust; (4) The trillion-dollar infrastructure buildout (data centers, power, chips) creates massive opportunities in the infrastructure layer while also flagging dependency risks; (5) AI safety being deprioritized by frontier labs creates both regulatory risk and opportunity for compliance-focused startups; (6) The report's finding that barriers have shifted from technological to 'social and material' (capital, politics, physics) means founders should focus less on model innovation and more on infrastructure access, regulatory positioning, and go-to-market execution.
entrepreneurial_relevance.actionable_insight: Founders should position products assuming near-universal enterprise AI adoption (44% paying and accelerating). The $530K average contract value suggests enterprise AI is a premium market — avoid race-to-bottom pricing. The China open-weights surge (Qwen, DeepSeek) means European and US founders must articulate their model supply chain and data sovereignty story clearly. The infrastructure bottleneck (power, chips, data centers) makes compute-efficient approaches a genuine competitive advantage. Safety deprioritization by labs creates space for trust-and-safety startups. Build for the application and vertical layers where value is accruing fastest.

confidence.cross_reference: Cross-referenced with Stanford HAI AI Index Report 2025 (https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report), CB Insights State of AI 2025 Report (https://www.cbinsights.com/research/report/ai-trends-2025/), DeepLearning.AI analysis (https://www.deeplearning.ai/the-batch/the-state-of-ai-report-2025-says-ais-barriers-arent-technological-but-social-and-material/), The Neuron summary (https://www.theneuron.ai/explainer-articles/state-of-ai-report-2025-trillion-dollar-bets-a-looming-power-crisis-and-chinas-ai-takeover), LessWrong discussion (https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/AvKjYYYHC93JzuFCM/2025-state-of-ai-report-and-predictions)
confidence.caveats: The report is produced by an AI venture capital investor (Nathan Benaich of Air Street Capital), which may introduce selection bias toward investable trends and technologies. The practitioner survey (n=1,200) is an open-access self-selected sample and may skew toward AI-enthusiastic professionals, not representative of the general workforce. The 44% US business AI adoption figure comes from Ramp (a corporate card company) data, which may overrepresent tech-forward companies. Many statistics are aggregated from third-party sources with varying methodologies. Ian Hogarth, previously co-author, transitioned to UK AI Safety Institute; his current involvement level in the 2025 edition may differ from earlier years. The report's predictions section is explicitly speculative.
confidence.measurement_reliability: analyst_estimate, survey_self_reported (practitioner survey is self-reported; industry metrics are analyst estimates compiled from multiple third-party sources; benchmark scores from standardized evaluations; adoption data from commercial analytics platforms like Ramp)
